explorationReceipt.approximateInspectedScope: Approximately 46 named tracks across two current 2026 releases, three adjacent 2021–2024 bass/breaks/electro windows and two overlooked 2011–2019 catalogues; attributed descriptions and metadata only; no audio audition.
exclusions: Canonical identities, active placement-specific rejects, untriggered PARKED revisits, previously retained exact identities, old unresolved leads without materially new identity evidence and release-level observations below the honest lead floor were excluded.
Second Storey — Disrupted Dialect was excluded because archived durable history shows the source lane was already inspected; only genuinely fresh source windows were retained.
The two listener-protected internal trio handoffs remain unavailable; Truth in Noise → Transparency and all other boundaries are not protected by implication.
The current 20-track length and Run 94 ADD are costs/signals, not a moratorium or an ADD quota.
No phrase structure, mixability, perceived pulse, scalar energy, density or felt state was invented beyond attributed descriptions.
rankedLeadSummary: 1. Bookworms — viz: Resident Advisor describes crunchy, spider-like drum programming supporting one of the album's catchiest chord sequences.
2. Microhm — Noise Treatment: the official release describes distortion compressed until it becomes pure pulse in a direct, physical 3:31 exercise.
3. Jason Hogans — For My Solids: Resident Advisor calls it a masterclass in chopped-up breaks, layering jazz elements through modern production.
4. Afrikan Sciences — Humanistic Center: Resident Advisor describes a tightly compressed machine-funk jam joining boogie, game-soundtrack colour and trance stabs.
5. Bookworms — slice of life: Resident Advisor documents slinky pulsing techno breaking into halftime hip-hop and reassembling as dubby bass.
6. Microhm — Broken Eucledeans: the official release describes fractured rhythms and unstable geometries in a concise 2:38 opening piece.
7. DJ Latinchat — Cafuné: Resident Advisor describes skittering percussion morphing into halftime strides through heavy sub-bass.
8. Vladislav Delay — Latoma: the official release describes gentle undulating dub-techno gradually evolving into a scuffed industrial breakbeat.

9. Koloah — Jump!: Mechatronica places the exact 5:07 track within a current electro EP of sharp programming, broken grooves, deep bass pressure and robotic voices; no track-specific behaviour is claimed.
